bib.title: LLMLingua: Compressing Prompts for Accelerated Inference of Large Language Models
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 2023 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), pages 13358-13376

question: Can a long prompt be compressed by a small language model, without gradients through the target LLM, to cut cost and latency at little loss in task performance?
hypothesis: Tokens with lower perplexity contribute less information, so dropping them (with a budget controller, iterative conditioning and distribution alignment) preserves the target LLM's behaviour at high compression ratios.
contributions: Coarse-to-fine prompt compression with a budget controller for demonstration/sentence-level selection
Iterative token-level compression (ITPC) modelling conditional dependence between compressed tokens
Instruction-tuning based distribution alignment between small LM and black-box LLM
Evaluation on GSM8K, BBH, ShareGPT and Arxiv-March23, claimed first to evaluate reasoning and ICL in efficient-LLM work

method.summary: A small LM (Alpaca-7B or GPT2-Alpaca) scores perplexity. A budget controller keeps high-perplexity demonstrations up to k*tau_dems*L_dems tokens and gives instruction and question a lighter ratio. ITPC then drops low-perplexity tokens segment by segment (segment size 100), conditioning on already compressed segments. The compressed prompt goes to a black-box LLM.
method.task: prompt compression for in-context learning, reasoning, conversation and summarisation

limits: Notable performance drop at excessively high compression ratios such as 25x-30x on GSM8K (Fig 3); the limit varies with prompt length, task type and sentence count.
Tokenizer differences between the small LM and the black-box LLM may underestimate token length.
Claude-v1.3 tested only at 1-shot and half-shot because of API cost.
GPT-3.5-Turbo could not restore compressed prompts; GPT-4 could (footnote 9, emergent-ability conjecture).
Tested on reasoning prompts, conversation and long-document summaries, not retrieved RAG passages.
No variance, seeds or significance tests; GPT-4 baseline reports the best of ten instructions.
Compressed prompts are hard for humans to read.
